title: Solve it: a recipe with a blank line
idea: GUIDED PROBLEM. Report a title then steps, using an empty print() to add a blank line for readability. Blank lines are part of the output plan.
problem: Show a recipe: the title Tea, then a blank line, then two steps — boil water, add tea bag.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: Show the title Tea, a blank line, then two steps (boil water, add tea bag).

How many lines of output in total (counting the blank line)?
exercises.explanation: Title (1) + blank line (1) + two steps (2) = 4 lines. The blank line counts as a line.

exercises.prompt: A blank line is still a line of output.
exercises.explanation: Yes. An empty line takes up a line on screen — it is part of the output you planned.

exercises.prompt: Example. Work the output by hand. Put these pieces in the order they should appear (the blank line is the gap).
exercises.explanation: Title, then the blank gap, then step one, then step two. This is the exact output to match.

exercises.prompt: Plan: which tool makes the blank line in the middle?
exercises.explanation: print() with nothing inside shows a blank line. You met this in Unit 1.

exercises.prompt: Plan: how many print instructions total (including the blank one)?
exercises.explanation: Title, blank, and two steps = four print instructions, one per line.

exercises.prompt: Code. Arrange the lines: title, blank, then the two steps.
exercises.explanation: print("Tea"), then print() for the gap, then the two step lines in order.

exercises.prompt: Build the instruction that makes the blank line.
exercises.explanation: print() with empty brackets shows a blank line — nothing between the brackets.

exercises.prompt:
Check. The output is:

Tea

boil water
add tea bag

Matches your example?
options: Yes — title, gap, two steps, in order
exercises.explanation: The blank line sits between the title and the steps, just as planned. Check passes.

exercises.prompt: If you forgot the empty print(), the title and the first step would end up on back-to-back lines with no gap.
exercises.explanation: Right. Removing the blank print removes the gap — the output no longer matches the example.

exercises.prompt: Why add a blank line at all?
options: To space the output out so it is easier to read
To make the program run faster
It is required by every program
exercises.explanation: Blank lines are for readability — they separate parts of the output cleanly.
